provenance.notes: Ext family batch. Extreme seasonal spike: the pitch lands in summer, the site sells in fall. Permanent roofline lighting is the year-round product. No light or controller brands named. Ranges are planning figures, not quotes.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Roofline only, roofline plus trees and bushes, wreaths and garland, full-property displays, and what each includes: lights, install, service calls, takedown and storage
pageStructurePlus.why: Buyers think in 'what will my house look like', not in feet of lights. Packages by house size let them pick and book in one sitting.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Install windows from fall into early December, takedown in January, storage of the customer's lights, and service calls when a strand goes out
pageStructurePlus.why: Install dates are the scarce thing in this trade. Showing the calendar early creates the urgency that fills it.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Low-profile track under the roofline, colours and patterns from a phone app, holidays, game days and everyday warm white, mounting on gutters and fascia, and power needs
pageStructurePlus.why: Permanent lighting is the big ticket and sells all year. Homeowners need to see the track by day and the effect by night to say yes.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Storefronts, office parks, HOA entrances, tall trees and town squares, lift equipment, insurance certificates and multi-year contracts
pageStructurePlus.why: Commercial displays are booked earlier and renewed yearly. Managers want capacity and insurance before they ask for a bid.

pageStructurePlus.contains: A mock-up of lights on the customer's house from a photo, warm white versus cool white versus multi-colour, and a design visit option for large properties
pageStructurePlus.why: Seeing the lit house before paying is what turns a maybe into a deposit, especially for first-time buyers.

designDirections.name: Book Your Install Date
designDirections.bestFor: Seasonal lighting crews selling roofline packages who need dates booked fast each fall
designDirections.headlineSample: Christmas light installation in {City}, dates going fast
designDirections.whyItFits: Ultramarine poster colours and a geometric display read like a seasonal campaign, and the page is a package picker and an install date form.

designDirections.name: Evergreen Glow
designDirections.bestFor: Established holiday lighting companies with a gallery of lit homes and a permanent lighting line
designDirections.headlineSample: Holiday and permanent lighting, installed and stored in {City}
designDirections.whyItFits: The family's own combo, and an easy fit: evergreen is the season's colour, and the calm serif reassures people letting a crew on their roof.

designDirections.name: After Dark
designDirections.bestFor: Premium crews selling permanent roofline lighting and estate-scale holiday displays
designDirections.headlineSample: Permanent roofline lighting that makes {City} homes glow
designDirections.whyItFits: A midnight ground and a Didone display let night photography carry the page, which is how lit homes look best.

openers.line: Your listing shows lit-up houses in the reviews but no website button. In October people start shopping for Christmas light installers and want to book a date, not wait for a callback.
openers.hook: Open their Maps listing and confirm there's no Website button. Screenshot it for when they reply.
openers.linkLine: A holiday lighting booking page for that button: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your lighting business lives on Facebook, which works in December. In the summer, when people research permanent roofline lighting, the page has nothing for them.
openers.hook: Tap their link and confirm it lands on Facebook. Note the last post date in the off-season.
openers.linkLine: A lighting site that sells all year: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your Christmas lighting site still shows last season's prices and a 'booking now' banner from last fall. People wonder whether this year's dates are even open.
openers.hook: Open the site and look for last year's dates or prices, or a free-host banner. Note which.
openers.linkLine: Same lighting company, updated for this season: {demo-link}

openers.angle: Night shots broken on a phone
openers.line: Your night photos of lit houses look muddy and cropped on my phone. The glow is the whole sale for holiday lighting, and it's lost on a small screen.
openers.hook: Only if they have a site. Load it on your phone and note what breaks. Screenshot it for when they reply.
openers.linkLine: Your holiday lighting gallery, built for phones: {demo-link}

openers.line: There's no way to see what roofline lighting costs without messaging you. A package picker by house size gets people to a deposit while they're excited.
openers.hook: Check their profile, listing and any site for package prices. If none, the angle holds.

openers.line: Your lit-up houses on Instagram are stunning, the warm white rooflines especially. They disappear into the feed by January, when they could sell next year's installs all summer.
openers.hook: Pick two lit houses on their grid you could describe by style. Mention one if they reply.
openers.linkLine: Your lit houses, kept front and centre all year: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your reviews love that you take the lights down and store them, so customers never untangle a strand again. That's the whole pitch for holiday lighting, and it stays on Google.
openers.hook: Read their reviews and copy one phrase about takedown, storage or no ladders. Quote it back.
openers.linkLine: Those holiday lighting reviews where buyers decide: {demo-link}

openers.line: Christmas light calendars fill early, and the companies taking deposits in summer start fall with a full schedule. A site built in July is ready when the searches start.
openers.hook: Use from June to August. Name the month in the reply.
openers.linkLine: Ready before Christmas lighting searches start: {demo-link}

openers.line: You've posted permanent roofline lighting jobs. People research those for weeks and want to see the track by daylight, the colours at night and how the app works, all on one page.
openers.hook: Only if they've posted permanent lighting. Note one job.
openers.linkLine: A permanent lighting page that answers every question: {demo-link}

openers.line: Saw you're hiring installers for the lighting season. Seasonal crew check whether a Christmas light company looks organised before they sign on for the ladder work.
openers.hook: Only if they posted a hiring note. Note the date.
openers.linkLine: A holiday lighting page with a careers section: {demo-link}

openers.line: Homeowners in {Neighborhood} type the town name next to 'holiday lighting company', and right now no page of yours answers for it, even if your crews already work there.
openers.hook: Find towns they mention in posts or reviews. Use the furthest.
openers.linkLine: A holiday lighting page for every town: {demo-link}

openers.line: You've posted lit storefronts and community entrances. Property managers book holiday displays in summer and want a page they can forward to the board.
openers.hook: Only if they've posted commercial or HOA displays. Note one.

openers.line: Christmas lighting means ladders on someone's roof in the cold. A page showing your insurance and how you clip to gutters without damage settles the worry.
openers.hook: Check whether they mention insurance anywhere. Never quote a policy you didn't see.
openers.linkLine: Insurance and safe installs on one lighting page: {demo-link}

openers.line: Once one house on a street is professionally lit, the neighbours ask who did it. Those people search the lighting company the next morning and find nothing to book.
openers.hook: Look for comments or reviews like 'neighbours keep asking'. Quote it back.
openers.linkLine: Where a neighbour's lighting referral would land: {demo-link}

openers.line: That {specific recent job} you posted is a beautiful lit roofline, crisp lines and even spacing. It should be the first thing anyone sees on a holiday lighting page.
openers.hook: Pick their newest lit house and name it: colour, style, and the street if tagged.
openers.linkLine: That lighting job, front and centre: {demo-link}

sequence.dm1:
Hi {Owner}, that {specific recent job} you posted is a gorgeous lit roofline, crisp and even.

I looked for Christmas light installers in {City} and found {Business Name} on social, but no site with package prices or a way to book an install date. I put together a sample holiday lighting site to see how it would look, with marked placeholders where your photos would go.

Want me to send it?
sequence.dm2:
{Owner}, following up in case my message got lost. Here's the sample lighting site for {Business Name}: {demo-link}

It has packages by house size, an install and takedown calendar with deposits, a permanent roofline lighting page and a commercial display page. If it's not for you, say so and I'll leave you be.
sequence.call:
"Hi, is this {Owner}? I'm {Your Name}, I build websites for holiday lighting companies in {City}. I messaged a couple of days ago, did it come through?"

IF NO:
"No problem. Short version: I built a sample site for {Business Name} where people pick a lighting package, see a price and put down a deposit for an install date, with marked placeholders where your photos would go. Can I text you the link?"

IF YES:
"What did you think?"
 → let them talk, don't fill the silence
"The build runs {Build Range} depending on packages and the permanent lighting page, then {Care Range} a month for hosting and seasonal changes. For a lighting company your size I'd quote about {Build Price}, a few roofline installs."
"Can I walk you through it for ten minutes this week? Summer is the right time to get it built."

CLOSE:
"I'll send a short scope and a deposit invoice. It'll be taking install deposits before the fall searches start."

objections.objection: I'm fully booked every December anyway.
objections.handler: "Then the site is about better jobs, not more. Deposits up front, bigger packages, and permanent lighting that pays in the months you're idle."

objections.objection: It's summer, nobody's thinking about Christmas lights.
objections.handler: "Exactly why now. You have time to build it, and it's ready the day people start searching."

objections.objection: My customers rebook by text every year.
objections.handler: "Keep that. The site handles the new ones, takes deposits so nobody flakes, and gives your regulars a one-tap rebook."

objections.objection: I'm on a lighting franchise's lead program.
objections.handler: "Those leads are shared or capped. Your own site sends people straight to you and keeps working after the program ends."
"Perfect. Happy to hand over the package picker layout. If it stalls before fall, the offer stands."
"{Build Range}. For you about {Build Price}, for packages, deposits, the install calendar and a permanent lighting page. A few installs pay it."

email.subject: Lighting site for {Business Name}

sequence.voicemail: "Hi {Owner}, {Your Name} here. I build websites for Christmas lighting companies in {City} and made a sample for {Business Name} that takes install deposits. I'll text the link. {Your Phone}. Thanks."
sequence.takedown:
{Owner}, I'm taking the {Business Name} lighting demo down on Friday.

Want me to keep it up? One word is fine.
sequence.nurture:
Hi {Owner}, holiday lighting searches are about to start, and install dates go fast once they do. Thought of you.

The lighting site's still here, same price. {demo-link} if you'd like another look.

bullets: Sell in summer; price the build against a few roofline installs, never against December's rush pricing.
Package picker with deposits is the core line; it's what turns December chaos into a booked calendar.
Permanent lighting gets its own page and price line; it's the year-round product with the biggest ticket.
Commercial display pages only for crews with lifts and commercial insurance.
Care plan covers seasonal swaps: booking banner in fall, takedown in January, permanent lighting in spring.
The mock-up request is cheap to add and lifts package size; include it when they can turn mock-ups around fast.

lineItems.description: Max with several package sizes, add-ons like wreaths and trees, deposit capture and install date selection.
Max with day and night views, an app pattern demo video and a quote form by roofline length.
Max with photo upload, colour choices and a turnaround promise on the page.
Max with a bid request form, insurance download and multi-year contract options.
Max when sorted by package and colour, with short clips of permanent lighting patterns.
Max when each town page shows lit homes there and its open install dates.

whatElseYouSell.name: Night lighting photo and video shoot
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "One evening shooting your best lit houses at dusk, when the sky is still blue, gives you next year's holiday lighting gallery and a season of posts."
whatElseYouSell.when: Early December, on their best installs.

whatElseYouSell.name: Google profile posts during lighting season
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "From October to December, lit houses and permanent lighting jobs go on your Google profile weekly with the town named, so the map shows a busy installer."

whatElseYouSell.name: Review asks the night the lights go on
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "The evening the Christmas lights first switch on, the homeowner gets a text asking for a review while the family's outside looking up."

whatElseYouSell.name: Early-bird booking campaign
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A late-summer offer to past customers and local groups to lock an install date with a deposit fills the holiday lighting calendar before competitors open."
whatElseYouSell.when: Pitch in July, run in August and September.

whatElseYouSell.name: Yard signs for lit houses
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A small lit-up yard sign saying who installed the lights is read by every car slowing down to look at the house."

whatElseYouSell.name: Neighbour cards on install day
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "While the crew is on the roof, the houses either side get a card with a same-street discount on Christmas lighting."

whatElseYouSell.name: Permanent lighting spring campaign
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "In spring, holiday customers hear about permanent roofline lighting, no more ladders next fall, with a quote link. It fills the quiet months."
whatElseYouSell.when: Pitch in February, run in March and April.

whatElseYouSell.name: Game-day and holiday pattern posts
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Posts showing permanent lighting customers' houses in team colours and holiday patterns keep the product visible all year."

withoutAI.route: Gutter crews who check before the lights go up
withoutAI.pitchLine: "Christmas light clips sit on gutters, so customers want gutters cleaned first. The gutter crew you refer needs a site too."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Same houses, same fall weeks, no overlap.

withoutAI.pitchLine: "Customers who love their holiday lighting ask about path and uplighting next. The landscape lighting installer you know needs a night-shot site."

withoutAI.whoPays: The electrician, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "Permanent lighting needs power in the right spot. The electrician who adds those outlets needs a site and sends you lighting jobs back."
"Event lighting companies string patio and tent lights all summer and refer holiday work in winter. They need a better site."

withoutAI.route: Shops and restaurants on the commercial route
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The storefronts you light every December have their own website problems, and they already trust you on their roof."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Small business owners need sites and see the client every season.

withoutAI.pitchLine: "People want the house clean before the holiday lights go up. The window cleaner you refer needs a booking site."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Pre-holiday cleaning is a natural pairing.

withAI.pitchLine: "Homeowners upload a yard photo and see path and uplighting previews, with permanent roofline lighting offered as an add-on."
"Event lighting companies get a bot that quotes tent and patio lighting by size and date, and refers holiday lighting in winter."
"An assistant drafts the community's holiday lighting plan, entrance, clubhouse and trees, with dates and vendor bids from one lighting company."
withAI.whyItWorks: Boards want it handled; the client gets a recurring contract.

withAI.pitchLine: "The gutter crew gets an assistant that books fall cleanings and offers your Christmas lighting install in the same message."
"A district assistant tracks which storefronts joined the holiday lighting program, sends reminders and routes installs to one crew."
withAI.whyItWorks: Districts want a unified street look with little admin.

withAI.pitchLine: "Electricians get a tool that drafts an exterior outlet quote from house photos, flagged for permanent lighting jobs."
withAI.whyItWorks: Faster electrical quotes speed permanent installs.

softwareAI.name: Missed-call text-back in lighting season
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Up on a roofline clipping lights in November? Callers get a text with the package picker link and the next open install dates."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Day 30, ideally before October. Needs their number forwarded.

softwareAI.name: Install and takedown date reminders
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Customers get a text before install day and before January takedown, so the gate's unlocked and the cars are moved."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs their install calendar.

softwareAI.name: Rebook-for-next-season deposits
softwareAI.pitchLine: "At takedown, every holiday lighting customer gets a link to lock the same install week next year with a small deposit."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: First January. Needs the deposit amount.

softwareAI.name: Holiday lighting review replies
softwareAI.pitchLine: "When a family posts that the house looks magical, a reply naming the roofline and colour they chose is ready for your thumbs-up."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: First season, with review asks. Needs a few past replies. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Lights-on-your-house mock-up
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Customers upload a daytime shot of the house and see it lit in warm white, cool white or colour, labelled as a preview, before choosing a package."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3, before fall. Needs their package styles. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Roofline footage draft from photos
softwareAI.pitchLine: "From street shots and an aerial view it drafts roofline length and peaks, so the lighting quote is close before anyone climbs."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs past measured houses. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Install route planner for the rush
softwareAI.pitchLine: "November installs grouped by neighbourhood and crew, so each truck lights a street a day instead of crossing {City}."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3, before the season. Needs booked addresses.

softwareAI.name: Light inventory and storage tracker
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Every customer's stored lights tagged by bin and house, with strand counts, so next year's install pulls the right box."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: First takedown season. Needs their storage system.

softwareAI.name: Service call tracker for dead strands
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Customers report a dark strand with a photo, and service calls queue by route, so the holiday lighting crew fixes several on one trip."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs their service policy.

softwareAI.name: Lighting season chatbot
softwareAI.pitchLine: "It answers 'do you use our lights or yours' and 'when do you take them down' at night, from your lighting policies, and books the package."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs their policies and packages. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Permanent lighting quote builder
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Enter roofline length, peaks and power points, and a permanent lighting quote with track, controller and install prints cleanly."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs their per-foot pricing.

softwareAI.name: Commercial display contract tracker
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Every storefront and HOA holiday display with its contract term, design, install date and renewal reminder in one place."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4, once they have commercial accounts.

softwareAI.name: Pattern scheduler support for permanent customers
softwareAI.pitchLine: "A simple page where permanent lighting customers request holiday and game-day patterns and see how-to videos, so support calls drop."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6, once permanent lighting jobs exist.

softwareAI.name: Lighting post and caption writer
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Captions for each lit house and permanent lighting pattern, drafted from job details and approved by you before posting."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs approval on every post. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Spoken roof walk to lighting quote
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Walk the house describing rooflines, trees and outlets, and a Christmas lighting quote draft is ready before you reach the truck."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs their quote template. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Crew safety and install checklist
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Crews tick off harness, ladder setup, clip spacing, timer test and a night check photo for every lit house."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Before the second season, when seasonal crew grows.

softwareAI.name: Season profit by package
softwareAI.pitchLine: "See which holiday lighting packages actually pay once lights, labour, service calls and storage are counted."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: After the first season. Needs receipts and crew hours.

softwareAI.name: Spring permanent lighting nudge
softwareAI.pitchLine: "After takedown, holiday customers with simple rooflines get a spring note about permanent lighting and a quote link."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: First spring. Needs the customer list.

softwareAI.name: Seasonal crew onboarding assistant
softwareAI.pitchLine: "New seasonal installers ask the assistant about clip types, ladder rules and route days from your lighting manual, instead of calling you on a roof."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Before the season. Needs their written procedures. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Seasonal installer applicant screener
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Seasonal lighting applicants say whether they're comfortable on roofs, can work evenings in the cold and have a ride, before you call."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Late summer hiring. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "I built a Christmas lighting package picker with deposits for one installer. Every lighting crew drowns in 'how much' messages in October."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Seasonal crews need it the same months everywhere.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Installer locator for a permanent lighting maker
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Homeowners who see permanent roofline lighting online want a local installer. A locator routes them to the crews who carry your track."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Makers sell through installers and need them found.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "When the wholesaler's counter gets asked who hangs holiday lights locally, a searchable pro list answers it and keeps those crews ordering there."

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Starter site for lighting franchise owners
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Holiday lighting franchises add territories every summer. Each needs local packages and an install calendar."
"Agencies with a holiday lighting client can license my package picker and permanent lighting template."
"Landscapers add Christmas lighting to fill winter. Sell them the package page, deposit flow and install calendar ready-made."
"Towns run tree lightings and downtown displays every year. A portal for sponsorships, schedules and contractor coordination saves staff time."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Municipal budgets exist for holiday programs.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: HOA holiday lighting portal across a management firm
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Every community gets an entrance display plan and an optional resident sign-up for home lighting, routed to one installer."
"New-home buyers add permanent roofline lighting in the options selector, and installs route to one lighting company."

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Early-bird campaign kit for lighting crews elsewhere
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "The summer deposit campaign, posts and texts, packaged for any holiday lighting crew."

routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: A lighting company in a new suburb
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Each suburb gets one holiday lighting client from me. {City} is lit; the brightest crew in the next suburb gets the demo in July."

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Rescue lighting sites stuck on last season
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Lots of lighting crews have a site frozen on last December. I rebuild it with packages and deposits before fall."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Owners already know they need it.

upsellLadder.offer: Lighting site build plus care plan, one contract
upsellLadder.trigger: They say yes to the demo, ideally in summer.
upsellLadder.line: "The holiday lighting site and care plan go on one contract, so the fall booking banner and January takedown notice are texts to me."

upsellLadder.trigger: The package picker is live and install dates are open.
upsellLadder.line: "The calendar is open. Let's fill the best Christmas lighting install weeks with deposits now."

upsellLadder.trigger: Enquiries ask what their house would look like before paying a deposit.
upsellLadder.line: "People want to see their house lit before they commit. The mock-up shows them."

upsellLadder.offer: Review asks the night the lights go on
upsellLadder.trigger: The first installs booked through the site are switched on.
upsellLadder.line: "The first Christmas lights booked through the site are on. Let's ask every family that night."

upsellLadder.offer: Night lighting photo and video shoot
upsellLadder.trigger: Several showpiece houses are lit in early December.
upsellLadder.line: "Your best holiday lighting jobs are up now. One evening at dusk fills next year's gallery."
"Takedown is the moment to lock next year's lighting install. Let's ask every customer then."

upsellLadder.trigger: Spring arrives with holiday customers who mentioned hating the ladders.
upsellLadder.line: "Your holiday customers never want to see a ladder again. Permanent lighting is the answer, and spring is the time."
